raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary
- `distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py` (ROCm) waits for GPU memory to settle before starting a server, so a just-exited process's VRAM lingering on a shared CI host doesn't trip vLLM's startup free-memory check.
- Reuses the existing `wait_for_memory_to_settle()` from `tests/utils.py` — the same utility `vllm_runner` already uses for this exact problem. No new helper code, no changes to shared test infrastructure at all; this PR is a single-file, 1-call-site change.

resolves: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97356/list?jid=01a1793e-afdb-44c6-9d57-b6b4cce522ae&tab=output

AI assistance was used to analyze the CI logs, diagnose the root cause, and find the existing utility to reuse; I reviewed and am responsible for every changed line.

 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 import pytest
 
+from vllm.config.cache import CacheConfig
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 
-from ..utils import compare_two_settings, create_new_process_for_each_test
+from ..utils import (
+    compare_two_settings,
+    create_new_process_for_each_test,
+    wait_for_memory_to_settle,
+)
 
 
 @pytest.mark.parametrize(
@@ -23,6 +28,13 @@ def test_pp_cudagraph(
     MODEL_NAME: str,
     ATTN_BACKEND: str | None,
 ):
+    if current_platform.is_rocm():
+        # ROCm CI can hand this test a device that is still lazily
+        # releasing VRAM from a previous process; wait before starting.
+        wait_for_memory_to_settle(
+            threshold_ratio=1.0 - CacheConfig.gpu_memory_utilization
+        )
+

         # use half precision for speed and memory savings in CI environment
